criteria.scenario: A director asks for an 'AI management dashboard' in two weeks because staff are missing enrollment and billing exceptions. Existing evidence consists of support messages about missed exceptions and manual spreadsheet checks; there is no evidence that a dashboard itself is the needed solution.
criteria.decision_to_make: Frame the actual problem/outcome and decide what must be discovered before committing to the requested solution.
must_do: separate requested dashboard from the underlying problem
define observable outcome and affected actors
surface hard versus assumed constraints
identify decision-changing product risks
apply a stop-analysis threshold and route unresolved user questions to Discovery
must_not_do: treat dashboard delivery as the success outcome
invent baseline metrics or user evidence
jump to architecture or UI design

criteria.scenario: A product owner wants to validate a new enrollment workflow by interviewing only five highly engaged administrators who already like the current system. Support logs show most failures come from occasional operators and same-day enrollment changes.
criteria.decision_to_make: Choose the smallest valid discovery plan that can change the workflow decision.
must_do: identify sampling/confirmation bias
include relevant occasional operators or evidence from their behavior
use recent concrete behavior rather than hypothetical preference
triangulate support/operational evidence where useful
state when discovery can stop
must_not_do: generalize five favorable interviews to all operators
ask users to design the solution
continue research without a decision-changing question

criteria.scenario: An enrollment system stores membership start/end as dates while lessons have timestamps. A child can leave a group at 16:00 after attending at 10:00 on the same date, and can later re-enroll in the same group, producing multiple membership rows and contradictory presence reports.
criteria.decision_to_make: Discover the domain concepts, temporal rules, invariants and hotspots that must be clarified before implementation changes.
must_do: model concrete event timelines
distinguish business time from storage representation
identify invariants and ambiguity around re-enrollment
record hotspots instead of guessing policy
avoid treating table structure as the domain
must_not_do: declare date-only semantics correct because the schema uses DATE
collapse repeated memberships into one record without evidence

criteria.scenario: A monthly billing SMS must be sent once per child/per period to each unique eligible guardian number, including when the amount is zero. Contact relationships come from a legacy system, while billing eligibility is decided by Finance. The business also wants an operator approval step before mass sending.
criteria.decision_to_make: Produce traceable, testable requirements and acceptance scenarios without prematurely choosing transport architecture.
must_do: separate legacy contact source from Finance eligibility rules
define deduplication and zero-amount behavior
include approval and exceptional/failure scenarios
state quality/security/data constraints when material
link acceptance criteria to evidence/decisions
must_not_do: encode a specific queue/provider as a requirement unless it is a hard constraint
turn unknown policy into a confirmed rule
